chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: Musicians as leaders of hip language and their intelligence
summary: Horace thinks musicians led hip language and that good musicians have high IQs, since playing demands concentration.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Do you think that -- again especially in those days and on into the '40's that the black musicians tended to be ahead of the average black person with regard to this use of this hip language?

Most of the hip language that even a lot of young people use today, whether they're white or black, we know has come from the black culture. But my question is do you think that the musicians were leaders in this or that it was common among, you know, the general black culture.

Well, I think the musicians were leaders, this. I think so. In fact, while we're talking about this, Tom, a lot of people that don't play music that are music lovers have often asked me certain questions about intelligence

of the musicians, you know, that play. Even now a lot of times -- like you'll get up and you'll fascinate some of your people with all this material. When you take your breaks and you begin to talk to them -- I know I've talked to certain people who operate in music -- he seems like a real nice fellow. Is he an educated fellow? I know he's educated with his instrument, you know, one of those things, but how is he as a person, one of those things.

And my reaction has always been, Well, I tell you, to my way of thinking and, I said, I don't want to be prejudiced in this thing, you know. I said, But to me the average musician that is good and produces actually has a very high IQ because in order to play an instrument, you've got to have a brilliant mind, you know, to know what you're doing, man.

And some of them like to hear you say this. Of course, there are that scant few that resent it, you know. I say, But, man, in order to play a horn, you've got to have your faculties about you to know what you're doing, and you've got to know what concentration means because that's actually what it's all about. And so they accept it, you know. But yet it fascinates them to know that, you know, they can talk intelligently to you and go right back and play the horn and knock them out.
